analysis:
Reviewed both files' metadata, patches and supplied source excerpts. The changes document explicit local rollback after promotion, single-predecessor retention, request draining, a journaled swap under the update lease, hash/signature verification, refusal during cluster/foreground/concurrent-update operation, and local quarantine with an explicit override (changelog.d/provider-update-rollback.md:3–7). docs/operations/provider-release.md:1033–1040 distinguishes release deactivation from local rollback; the patch retains the separate permanent-build-revocation warning. No executable controls change in these units, and offline rollback does not itself establish serving permission or bypass coordinator policy. No independently supported security regression was identified.
Integration should verify the documented behavior against updater/watchdog implementation, especially retained-artifact identity and race resistance, drain/force semantics, crash recovery, and quarantine persistence across startup, periodic checks and watchdog recovery (T-043, A-018). Restored builds must still obtain fresh connection-bound authorization and remain subject to qualification/revocation (TB-002, TB-009, T-052–T-054, A-017); local signature validity is not serving authorization. Shared fan-helper downgrade compatibility is relevant because the unchanged release guide notes older providers lack the newer-helper replacement check (docs/operations/provider-release.md:488–496; T-047). These are unverified integration contracts, not findings based on imagined historical deployments. Implementation and unchanged callers are not supplied in this batch; selected threat definitions, rather than every definition's full detail, were available.
